title: Car extended warranty messages: Scams or just misleading?
summary: A local TV investigation calls car warranty renewal mailers and calls misleading rather than illegal, showing a reporter's own 'upgrade' pitch turning out to add almost nothing.

assertions.quote: Even if you buy a brand new car, you could still get. These mailers.

verdicts.note: Telemarketing lead lists aren't filtered by actual warranty status, so these mailers commonly reach people with active coverage.

assertions.quote: The letters are alarming with words like important and personal and confidential open immediately.

verdicts.note: This alarming-language tactic is a well-documented feature of these mailers, confirmed by BBB and FTC reporting.

FTC gives example urgent-sounding scam phrases ("Motor Vehicle Notification," "Final Warranty Notice," "Notice of Interruption") used "to make the offer seem urgent," matching the mechanism though not the exact wording ("important," "confidential") the claim names.

assertions.quote: That's only 1000 miles more of warranty coverage. But nearly 4 months.

verdicts.note: Investigative calls routinely find the actual extra coverage offered is trivial relative to the pitch.

assertions.quote: For the big ticket items you want to avoid having double coverage.

verdicts.note: An extended warranty purchased before the factory warranty expires mostly overlaps with existing coverage until the factory term ends.
Same FTC guidance: a service contract that starts before the manufacturer's warranty expires "probably won't help," i.e. it duplicates coverage already in force.

assertions.quote: Never make a decision in the moment.

verdicts.note: Fraud-prevention experts consistently flag urgency pressure as a scam indicator, though legitimate telemarketers can also be pushy.

FTC says scam callers "pressure you to give them personal financial information and a down payment right away, before they give you details" -- consistent with immediate-decision pressure being a scam hallmark.

assertions.quote: If you no longer have your manufacturer's warranty in place, this may be something you want to consider.
